Solution 2 is correct: the minimal axis ratio is 11/3.

I checked Solution 2's setup. The conic family x² + (112/33)xy + ty² − 130x − 33ty = 0 passes through all four vertices. The ratio of semi-axes is √(λ₂/λ₁) for the eigenvalues of the quadratic-form matrix, which gives λ₂/λ₁ = (u+s)/(u−s) with u = 1+t and s = √((u−2)² + (112/33)²). Writing g = s²/u² = 1 − 4/u + (4+k²)/u² with k = 112/33, the minimum over 1/u is at g = k²/(4+k²). Since 4+k² = (130/33)², this gives s/u = 56/65, so λ₂/λ₁ = (121/65)/(9/65) = 121/9 and the axis ratio is 11/3. The critical t also satisfies the ellipse condition.

Solution 1 uses an equivalent coordinate placement but reaches (65+√5314)/33 ≈ 4.17, so it contains an error. Solution 3 is a long numerical search that lands near 3.67, which is 11/3 rounded to two decimals, not the exact value.
